 CINCINNATI (WKRC) — Todd Benzinger, the former Cincinnati Reds first baseman who caught the final out of the franchise’s 1990 World Series victory, has died. He was 63.
 The Reds announced Benzinger’s death Thursday. No cause of death was released. 
 View post on X 
 Benzinger spent three seasons with Cincinnati from 1989 through 1991 and played a key role on the Reds team that led the National League West from start to finish before sweeping the Oakland Athletics in the 1990 World Series.
 He secured the final out of that series, a moment that made him part of one of the most celebrated teams in franchise history.
 “Todd will forever be remembered by Reds fans for catching the final out of the 1990 World Series, but those of us who had the privilege of knowing him will remember so much more,” Rick Walls, executive director of the Reds Hall of Fame and Museum, said in a statement. “Todd remained close to the Cincinnati community and was a tremendous friend to the Reds Hall of Fame and Museum, generously participating in our events and sharing his time with fans. We will miss his friendship, his kindness and his presence in our community.”
 Benzinger was born in Dayton, Kentucky, and graduated from New Richmond High School in Ohio. The Boston Red Sox selected him in the second round of the 1981 MLB draft, and he made his major league debut with Boston in 1987 before joining the Reds ahead of the 1989 season.
 After his playing career, Benzinger remained closely connected to the Cincinnati area. He managed the Class A Dayton Dragons from 2009 to 2010 and spent years coaching and mentoring young baseball players in the New Richmond community.
 The Reds said Benzinger regularly supported the organization through the Reds Hall of Fame and Museum and the Reds Community Fund. He also participated in Reds Caravan, Reds Fantasy Camp, Reds Legends Remember and Redsfest events.
